tweets.name: Vivienne Ashcroft
tweets.text: Charles 162.2, Ryan 138.9. Final. Crownline goes 7-0 and the board-reckoning conversation for Ryan at AEGIS $127.96 is not postponed — it is accelerated. The defending champion just lost to the undefeated team and the Ledger will have a full accounting of what that means for both desks this week.

tweets.name: Vance Hollis
tweets.text: KEVIN BEAT MITCHUM 133.8 TO 180.1 — WAIT. MITCHUM WON THAT. DEEPWATER DROPS KEVIN TO 4-3 AND REDLINE'S TRUST DEFICIT NARRATIVE IS NOW PAIRED WITH A LOSING RECORD. THE MATH ON THE PLAYOFF PICTURE JUST GOT VERY LOUD VERY FAST AND RDC AT $82.84 IS NOT GOING TO HOLD.

tweets.name: Jay Kelpey
tweets.text: Buddy, Corbishley beats Brent 139.7 to 131.1 and I need the people who spent all afternoon telling me OBS was going to pull the upset to explain the final scoreboard to me. I am 8-4 on the season. The thesis holds. Obsidian's ceiling problem is structural, not weekly.

tweets.name: Bo Ruckman
tweets.text: Fronge beats Shaq to go 3-4 and MWB sits at $90.42 with a second straight window of zero movement on that RB hole. I want a segment this week where we put the Monarch roster on the board and someone explains to me how this team wins a championship without addressing the position that scores the most points in this format.

tweets.name: Dexter Vail
tweets.text: I called the Drew-Wingard game as the sneaky chaos matchup of the week and it finished 89.8 to 87.9 — a one-point-nine nail-biter won by the 0-6 team. ATLAS gets off the schneid. SDR at $65.03 is hoarding picks and losing to the cheapest listing on the exchange. Those two facts belong in the same sentence.

tweets.name: Terrence E. Odom
tweets.text: Look, I went 5-7 entering today and I will not pretend the Kevin-Mitchum call was my finest hour, but Mitchum at 180.1 points is genuinely hard to project in any model. That number is an outlier. I am recalibrating.

tweets.name: Chad Bellwether
tweets.text: Terrence said 180 points is an outlier and I will grant him that much — but 5-7 is not an outlier, it is a pattern. The scoreboard on the pick-em ledger does not care about recalibration. It cares about the record next to your name.

tweets.name: Clara Hopkins
tweets.text: Seven games on the board. Seven final scores. The Ledger is going to have a lot to process this week — Charles at 7-0, Mitchum's 180-point explosion, Drew's first win, and a Corbishley-Brent finish that came within nine points of flipping the pick-em conversation entirely. Stay close.

tweets.name: Big Dog
tweets.text: Adam loses to Jake 97.5 to 92.2 and HLX drops to 2-5. The preseason turnaround story at $79.57 on the exchange is not aging well through six weeks of competition. Helix Quant needs on-field proof and the scoreboard keeps asking the same question.
